decisive_items: Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot showed no thickening of the plantar fascia and no signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow. However, MRI revealed a pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus, measuring approximately 1.1 cm × 0.9 cm.
non-specific tenderness over the plantar aspect of the calcaneus at the insertion of the plantar fascia
response.rationale: MRI demonstrates a pedunculated calcaneal bony protrusion without plantar fascia thickening or adjacent signal alteration, best matching a plantar calcaneal enthesophyte. Other candidates are contradicted by normal plantar fascia imaging or describe a different location or contributing finding.

rejected.why: Plantar fascial fibromatosis would show plantar fascia thickening or nodularity on MRI, which is explicitly absent.
Plantar fasciitis is not supported because MRI shows no plantar fascia thickening or signal alteration.
Haglund syndrome involves a posterosuperior calcaneal prominence, not a posterolateral plantar bony protrusion.
Gastrocnemius tightness is an associated examination finding but does not explain the discrete calcaneal bony protrusion.
